scenario: AITA for refusing to loan my brother my vacation money? | My (21F) brother (30M) and I live with our parents. He’s in a shitty job trying to get out so he went back to school and that’s why he moved back in 1 1/2 years ago. I’m in third year university and working to put myself through. I’m in business school which I am finding to difficult but not impossible. I should graduate in 2 years. When I got into uni I started saving for a bit of all my paycheques (whatever I could manage; sometimes it was as much as 15% and others as low as 1%) to go on a big vacation post uni gradation. Probably a cruise, Japan or a trip to different countries in Europe I’ve never been to. It has about $2800 in it now. My brother has not been on a vacation in many years and keeps hinting that he needs one. My parents already help him financially so he wouldn’t ask them for more help for that. Last week when he was complaining to my parents about it, they mentioned me and my vacation fund and said he could’ve been doing that all these years to be able to afford to go somewhere, or he could start now and maybe be able to go across country in a year. 3 days ago he came to me and asked if he could borrow my vacation money to go on a trip to Japan this summer or Fall. He said since I won’t need it for another 2 years it’s plenty of time for him to pay me back. I said no. My brother is horrible with money. He makes about as much as I do yet always seems to be broke despite never buying groceries or paying rent (for the record, I do not pay rent either, which is why I have been able to build up the fund, but I do buy most of my own groceries, as well as pay for all my makeup, health supplies, phone and uni fees). He’s very mad I said no. He says it’s jor fair as the youngest child I got to go away with mom and dad more while he had to go to college or work because he had moved out and was older. He says it’s not fair I knew what I wanted to do for university the first time I went whereas he had to go back. He says I’ve only been able to save so much money because “mom and dad spoiled me.” I disagree. My father, as well as my uni accounting and finance classes taught me to budget. If anything I think my parents spoiled him Because doesn’t know how to do much of anything for the real world outside his actual job. I don’t think it’s fair for me to have to give up my vacation money to him. I doubt he will be able to pay me back in time. Even if he couldn’t roger he could... I’m uncomfortable. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being AITA (A**hole in The Arena) for refusing to loan my brother my vacation money. Let me start by understanding the situation. My brother and I live with our parents. He's 30 and went back to school after a bad job, moving back in about 11 months ago. I'm 21, in my third year of university, working to put myself through business school, which is tough but manageable. I plan to graduate in two years. When I started university, I began saving a bit from each paycheck, sometimes 15%, other times as low as 1%, to go on a big vacation after graduation. I'm looking at a cruise, Japan, or a trip to Europe. My savings are around $2800 now. My brother hasn't been on a vacation in many years and keeps hinting he needs one. Our parents already help him financially, so he wouldn't ask them for more. Last week, when he was complaining to my parents about needing a vacation, they mentioned my vacation fund and suggested he could start saving now to maybe go somewhere in a year. Three days ago, he came to me and asked to borrow my vacation money to go to Japan this summer or fall. He said since I won't need it for another two years, there's plenty of time for him to pay me back. I said no. My brother is horrible with money. He makes about the same as I do but always seems broke despite never buying groceries or paying rent (we both don't pay rent, which is why I've been able to save up). I buy most of my groceries, makeup, health supplies, phone, and uni fees. He's very mad at me for saying no. He says it's not fair because as the youngest, I get to go away with mom and dad more while he had to go to college or work because he moved out and was older. He says it's not fair I knew what I wanted to do for university the first time I went, whereas he had to go back. He also says I've only been able to save so much because mom and dad spoiled me. I disagree. My father, as well as my university accounting and finance classes, taught me to budget. I think my parents spoiled him because he doesn't know how to do much for the real world outside his job. I don't think it's fair for me to give up my vacation money to him. I doubt he'll be able to pay me back on time, even if he could. I'm feeling uncomfortable about this. Is AITA? Alright, so I need to figure out if I'm being AITA. Let's break it down. First, what's AITA? It's when someone is being unnecessarily harsh or unreasonable in a situation, often involving family or friends. So, is my refusal to lend my brother money unreasonable? Let's look at the reasons I said no: 1. He's bad with money. He makes the same as me but is always broke. He doesn't manage his finances well. 2. He's not contributing to the fund. I've been saving for years, and he hasn't helped me. 3. He's asking to borrow money for a vacation, which is a non-essential expense. 4. I don't think he'll be able to pay me back on time, which could cause problems for me. 5. My parents already help him financially, so he shouldn't be asking me. On the other hand, my brother feels it's unfair because I'm the youngest and have had more opportunities. He's been through more, having to go back to school and move back in. He feels I've been spoiled, and he's entitled to some of my savings. But is that a valid reason? I don't think so. My savings are for my future, and I've worked hard to accumulate them. He's an adult, and while he's struggling, he should be responsible for his own finances. Also, my parents are already helping him, so it's not my responsibility to bail him out again. I've set boundaries with my money, and I should stick to them. I'm also concerned about the precedent. If I lend him money and he doesn't pay back, it could strain our relationship further. Plus, I need that money for my own plans, which I've been saving for a long time. So, considering all this, I don't think I'm being AITA. I'm setting a reasonable boundary, protecting my own financial goals, and not enabling his poor money habits. It's tough, but sometimes you have to prioritize yourself, especially when it comes to money and family.
